extracted.intended_audience: students and public relations practitioners (PR professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, stepwise approach for designing, implementing and managing public relations campaigns of varying sizes, with attention to research, objectives, strategy, tactics, resourcing and evaluation. Emphasises a 12-step planning model and contemporary developments such as social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12-step (12-point) planning model
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a revised and more dynamic 12-step (described as a 12-point plan) planning model to implement and run a campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book presents a 12-point plan/12-step planning model intended as a blueprint for campaigns of all sizes to ensure successful implementation and management. It is the central organising framework for planning and managing PR campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good planning and effective management
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful campaigns depend on good planning and effective management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Getting a public relations campaign or programme off the ground can seem overwhelming, but as with any project the secret of success lies in good planning and effective management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of PR in organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and articulate the role of public relations within the organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning should start from clarity about PR's role in the organisational context so that campaigns align with organisational goals and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of context
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse the contextual environment in which the campaign will operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context is vital — understanding political, cultural, sectoral and stakeholder contexts shapes appropriate objectives, messages, strategy and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct rigorous research and analysis to inform campaign decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and analysis underpin objective setting, audience identification, message development and evaluation; it is presented as an early and essential stage in the planning model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply relevant communication theory to inform strategy and message design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication theory is included among the vital topics to help practitioners design effective messaging and select appropriate communication channels and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Set clear objectives for the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective-setting is a discrete planning step; objectives should be clear and guide subsequent choices about publics, content, strategy, tactics, timescales and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publics and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify target publics and develop suitable content for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The planning model treats publics (audiences) and content as linked components — messages and content must be tailored to the identified publics to achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy and tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop coherent strategy and select appropriate tactics to implement it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy defines the overall approach while tactics are the specific activities (media relations, events, social media activity etc.) used to deliver the strategy; both are core elements of the 12-step plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timescales and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan realistic timescales and allocate resources needed to deliver the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timescales and resources are treated as a planning dimension to ensure campaigns are deliverable and sustainable; resource planning includes staffing, budget and logistical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate campaign outcomes and conduct review to inform future practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and review are final stages of the planning model — campaigns should include mechanisms for measuring success against objectives and learning for future campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate social media developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for and use contemporary social media developments in campaign planning and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The updated edition includes new coverage of key social media developments, signalling that modern campaigns must integrate social media strategy, platforms and measurement into planning, tactics and evaluation.
